tagline: Up the Saco on an Abenaki path, then over the notch.
intro: Route 113 leaves Standish and follows the Saco valley northwest, running through the center of Steep Falls together with Route 11, then on through Hiram and Brownfield to Fryeburg. This was the Pequawket Trail, the path of the Sokokis Abenaki from Standish to their stockaded village at Fryeburg. The name meant "crooked place", for the big bend the river makes there.
Past Fryeburg the road turns north along the New Hampshire line, crosses into New Hampshire and back out twice, and climbs through Evans Notch toward Gilead.

moments.title: Hiram
moments.text: First called Great Ossipee and then named for the biblical king of Tyre, Hiram kept a stage stop on the old trail and later a junction of two railroads.

moments.title: Jockey Cap, Fryeburg
moments.text: A half-mile trail climbs this granite glacial erratic by the Saco to a bronze cast of the profile survey Robert Peary made of the hills and mountains in view from the top.

moments.title: Evans Notch
moments.text: At 1,410 feet the road crosses the easternmost notch through the White Mountains, with the Royces to the west and Speckled Mountain to the east.
